title: Metal screw, ceramic insulation
bullets: Metal screw carries the tensile load
Screw and small metal washer are electrically live
Alumina separates them from the grounded body
Main PTFE sealing ring stays in place
speech: This proposal keeps the metal screw. There are no PEEK screws. The screw threads into the live steel spacer, so the screw and the small metal washer under its head are also live. The blue Boden is grounded. The cream coloured ceramic pieces isolate those metal parts from the Boden. This is a section through one actual screw position, with the surrounding source geometry cropped for clarity.

title: Two simple ceramic parts
bullets: Thick ceramic washer isolates the head
Small metal washer spreads head contact
speech: The proposed insulator has two separate ceramic pieces. An alumina tube surrounds the shank through the grounded body. A thicker alumina washer supports the screw head through a small metal washer. The ceramic is not threaded. The parts are separated sideways here to show their shapes, not to prescribe a removal path. This arrangement avoids asking a plastic screw to hold the assembly together.

title: What needs to change
bullets: Head pocket enlarged: 8 to 12 mm in this concept
Flat supported ceramic seat; controlled tightening
Metal M3 x35 retained; nominal entry depth 5 mm
RF clearances and ceramic stress still to verify
speech: This is not a drop in ceramic copy of the thin Teflon flange. The local head pocket is enlarged from eight to twelve millimetres to support a wider ceramic washer. Its seat must be flat, and tightening must be controlled to avoid damaging the ceramic. The concept retains an M three by thirty five metal screw. The thicker bearing stack leaves five millimetres of nominal entry into the live spacer, before allowing for the entry chamfer. Final thread strength, ceramic stress and RF clearances remain to be checked. The main Teflon sealing ring remains in the clamping stack, so this change does not eliminate all polymer creep.
